messages:
EvalBot: Nightly eval finished for model: rwd-v2-3b-quant, run_id=2026-06-15T03:00Z. Overall pass rate -6.3% vs baseline. Failing prompt ids: [A128, B204, C077].

Maya Chen: noticed the drop correlates with sampling config change in yesterday's deploy (temp default bumped 0.2->0.7 for AB test). quick triage: failures are mostly hallucination-y rewrites.

Liam O'Connor: can you paste a few failure examples?

Maya Chen: sure — example (prompt A128):
```
Q: Summarize the policy for data retention.
A: The retention period is 30 days.
```
Model output (baseline temp=0.2): "Data is retained for 30 days per policy."
Model output (current nightly, temp=0.7): "We usually keep data for a month but sometimes longer, depends on team decisions." -> introduces vagueness.

Dina Patel: that's consistent with higher temperature producing more diverse/less factual outputs. But why would nightly evals flip only for certain prompts?

Samir Rao: two hypotheses: 1) sampling param change alone, 2) random seed treatment changed in quantized runtime (we recently merged a PR that touched RNG state in CUDA kernels).

Maya Chen: timeline: deploy at 02:20 had default sampling temp update. PR #4123 at 02:05 touched kernel RNG init (seed per worker). Nightly run used new binary. So both changes coincident.

Liam O'Connor: can we re-run small batch with only temp change (old runtime) and with only runtime change (old temp) to isolate?

Maya Chen: started a quick matrix (3 prompts x 20 seeds each):
- control: runtime=v1.23, temp=0.2
- temp-only: runtime=v1.23, temp=0.7
- rng-only: runtime=v1.24, temp=0.2
- both: runtime=v1.24, temp=0.7

Maya Chen: preliminary results: temp-only shows increased variance but mean pass drop ~4%. rng-only shows odd repeatability issues: several seeds produce systematically different outputs for same seed across inferences (seed 42 -> two distinct outputs in separate runs). both shows worst drop ~7%.

Dina Patel: seed non-determinism is a red flag. If RNG isn't deterministic across runs the eval harness can't attribute regressions to parameters. Do we log the per-request randstate?

Samir Rao: we do log a short rng hash in debug mode. checked logs for run_id 2026-06-15T03:00Z: worker-3 rng_hash changed between step 1 and 2 within same session. suspect thread-local PR in #4123 reinitializes RNG on micro-batches.

Liam O'Connor: action items:
- Samir: revert PR or patch RNG init to be deterministic across micro-batches (hotfix candidate).
- Maya: re-run nightly eval with temp pinned to 0.2 on current runtime to confirm isolation.
- Dina: collect per-prompt seed sensitivity curves (temp sweep 0.0/0.2/0.5/0.7 + top_p 0.9/0.95 + top_k 40/80) for failing prompts.

Maya Chen: created jobs: j-5567 (temp pinned), j-5568 (repro matrix). ETA ~45m.

EvalBot: Job j-5567 completed. Summary: pass rate returned to baseline when temp pinned to 0.2 on v1.24 (runtime with RNG bug). Means temp change explains ~4% but remaining ~3% traced to RNG non-determinism.

Samir Rao: pushed a small patch that moves RNG seeding to session start and adds assert that seed is unchanged across micro-batches. Patch: https://git.internal/r/PR/4189

Dina Patel: once patch lands can we re-run quick check: same seed should produce identical token streams. Test snippet:
```
# run twice
out1 = generate(model, prompt, seed=1234)
out2 = generate(model, prompt, seed=1234)
assert out1.tokens == out2.tokens
```
If fails -> RNG still mutates between invocations.

Liam O'Connor: also add a small eval metric: seed_stability = fraction of seeds that produce deterministic output across 3 repeats. Nightly should assert seed_stability >= 0.995.

Maya Chen: agreed. filing a follow-up ticket for dashboard alert.

Samir Rao: PR merged, will roll to canary. will monitor eval logs.

Maya Chen: thanks all. main takeaway: temperature increase accounts for the majority but hidden nondeterminism in RNG amplified failures and made regressions sticky.

Dina Patel: thumbs up. will update the regression playbook to include seed_stability checks and to never change runtime RNG code without a non-regression check. :white_check_mark:

Liam O'Connor: nice triage. if canary looks good we should unpin temp and run a proper A/B with seeded runs to measure true user-facing delta.

EvalBot: Canary roll complete on subset infra. Seed_stability metric for canary: 0.998. Nightly re-run scheduled at 08:00Z to validate full regressions.
